newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh prepares for foreign leaders' visit.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh prepares for foreign leaders' visit.

text.p: Bangladesh is tightening security for the visits of the South African, Turkish and Palestinian presidents who arrive in Dhaka on Tuesday to attend celebrations marking the country's independence anniversary.
"We are putting all our strength to ensure fool-proof security for the (foreign leaders). It will be a gigantic task," one senior security official told Reuters on Monday.
"After all, Bangladesh has little experience simultaneously entertaining more than one international personality," he said.
South African President Nelson Mandela, President Suleyman Demirel of Turkey and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will join the celebrations to be held on Wednesday.
Bangladesh proclaimed independence from Pakistan on March 26, 1971, and was finally liberated on December 16 the same year after a nine-month war with help from India.
The three leaders would also meet separately with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Tuesday to discuss economic and others issues, foreign ministry officials said.
"There will be important talks on economic relations, especially during the meeting with President Demirel," one official said.
Demirel will be accompanied by a large trade delegation.
Bangladesh is expected to join a Turkey-sponsored trade bloc of eight Islamic countries due to be launched in July.
All three leaders will stay at the Dhaka Sheraton Hotel, foreign ministry officials said, an arrangement which could complicate security due to the presence of other hotel guests.
They will fly to the independence war mausoleum at Savar, 40 km (25 miles) from Dhaka, early on Wednesday to lay wreaths.

Later, they will attend an independence day anniversary function at Dhaka's historic Suhrawardy garden, where the country's independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Rahman called for resistance against the Pakistani army on March 7, 1971.
Mujib, father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the first president of Bangladesh, was assassinated with most of his family in a military coup in August, 1975.
The foreign leaders will leave Dhaka on March 27.
